channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: CURUPIRA: Clever guard for harm and linguistic prompt mitigation in Brazilian Portuguese
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a linguistic prompt mitigation/guard mechanism named CURUPIRA for Brazilian Portuguese.
  • Targets harmful behavior by adding a “guard” layer to reduce prompt-driven harm in Portuguese.
  • Focuses on mitigation rather than discovering or measuring attacks against model safety.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Rogério Sousa, William Alberto Cruz-Castañeda, José Roberto Homeli Silva', 'Marcellus Amadeus']
  • Tags: ['prompt-mitigation', 'guardrails', 'harm prevention', 'linguistic safety', 'Portuguese (Brazilian)']

item.title: SyncBreaker:Stage-Aware Multimodal Adversarial Attacks on Audio-Driven Talking Head Generation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SyncBreaker, a stage-aware multimodal protection framework for audio-driven talking-head (diffusion-based) generation.
  • Introduces two defenses: MIS nullifying supervision for the image stream to drive outputs toward a static portrait, and CAF to suppress audio-conditioned cross-attention in specific diffusion intervals.
  • Optimizes image and audio perturbations under modality-specific perceptual constraints and combines them at inference time.
  • Evaluates in a white-box proactive protection setting, showing degraded lip synchronization/facial dynamics while preserving perceptual quality and robustness under purification.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Wenli Zhang', 'Xianglong Shi', 'Sirui Zhao', 'Xinqi Chen', 'Guo Cheng', 'Yifan Xu', 'Tong Xu', 'Yong Liao']
  • Tags: ['Multimodal security', 'Adversarial attacks', 'Diffusion-stage attacks', 'Audio-driven generation', 'Proactive model/data perturbation']

item.title: HaloProbe: Bayesian Detection and Mitigation of Object Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies hallucination detection and mitigation in vision-language models by modeling object hallucination probabilities.
  • Identifies unreliability of attention-based detection due to confounders (token position and object repetition) causing Simpson’s paradox.
  • Proposes HaloProbe, a Bayesian framework combining external description statistics with internal decoding signals to estimate token-level hallucination likelihood.
  • Uses HaloProbe as an external scoring signal for non-invasive mitigation via guided decoding, improving hallucination rates while preserving utility.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Reihaneh Zohrabi', 'Hosein Hasani', 'Akshita Gupta', 'Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah', 'Anna Rohrbach', 'Marcus Rohrbach']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'vision-language models', 'hallucination detection', 'Bayesian methods', 'robust decoding']

item.title: Towards Context-Aware Image Anonymization with Multi-Agent Reasoning
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents CAIAMAR, a context-aware, agentic image anonymization framework for PII that is sensitive to spatial/property context.
  • Uses diffusion-based anonymization guided by multi-agent reasoning (PDCA loop) with coarse-to-fine detection and segmentation to capture both direct and indirect identifiers.
  • Evaluates effectiveness via person re-identification risk reduction and image quality metrics, and emphasizes on-premise, auditable outputs for GDPR transparency.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Robert Aufschl\\"ager', 'Jakob Folz', 'Gautam Savaliya', 'Manjitha D Vidanalage', 'Michael Heigl', 'Martin Schramm']
  • Tags: ['AI security privacy', 'Image anonymization', 'Re-identification risk', 'Diffusion-based obfuscation', 'GDPR/PII protection']

item.title: Adversarial Evasion Attacks on Computer Vision using SHAP Values
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a white-box adversarial evasion attack for computer vision models that uses SHAP values at inference to identify influential input features.
  • Demonstrates that the attack can reduce model output confidence and cause misclassifications with adversarial perturbations that are intended to be imperceptible to humans.
  • Compares the SHAP-based attack against FGSM and reports improved robustness for inducing misclassifications, especially under gradient-hiding/defenses.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Frank Mollard', 'Marcus Becker', 'Florian Roehrbein']
  • Tags: ['adversarial evasion', 'computer vision', 'white-box attack', 'SHAP-based attacks', 'gradient hiding']

item.title: Out-of-the-box: Black-box Causal Attacks on Object Detectors
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces BlackCAtt, a black-box causal attack method for object detectors using minimal, causally sufficient pixel sets.
  • Targets explainable, imperceptible, and reproducible adversarial perturbations that are architecture-agnostic.
  • Evaluates against standard black-box adversarial attack methods, including improvements when model confidence is available.
  • Finds that causal pixel targeting yields smaller and less perceptible attacks while maintaining success rate.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Melane Navaratnarajah', 'David A. Kelly', 'Hana Chockler']
  • Tags: ['adversarial-examples', 'black-box-attack', 'object-detection', 'causal-explainability']

item.title: PRADA: Probability-Ratio-Based Attribution and Detection of Autoregressive-Generated Images
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes PRADA, a probability-ratio-based method to detect and attribute autoregressive-generated images.
  • Uses the ratio between conditional and unconditional probabilities of the token sequence representing an image as a model-specific signature.
  • Calibrates a simple thresholded score function for detection and attribution across multiple AR image generators.
  • Demonstrates effectiveness experimentally against multiple class-to-image and text-to-image AR models; releases code/data.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Simon Damm', 'Jonas Ricker', 'Henning Petzka', 'Asja Fischer']
  • Tags: ['AI-generated-image detection', 'Attribution', 'Autoregressive image generation', 'Probability-based scoring', 'Model fingerprinting']

item.title: How Noise Benefits AI-generated Image Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies robustness of AI-generated image detection under out-of-distribution conditions.
  • Identifies spurious shortcut features exploited during training as a key weakness.
  • Proposes PiN-CLIP, a method that learns feature-space positive-incentive noise to suppress shortcut-sensitive directions and amplify stable forensic cues.
  • Evaluates on an open-world dataset of synthetic images from many generative models and reports improved detection accuracy.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ziqiang Li', 'Jiazhen Yan', 'Fan Wang', 'Kai Zeng', 'Zhangjie Fu']
  • Tags: ['AI-generated image detection', 'Robustness', 'Out-of-distribution generalization', 'Feature-space perturbations', 'CLIP']

item.title: Unmasking Puppeteers: Leveraging Biometric Leakage to Disarm Impersonation in AI-based Videoconferencing
item.description:
Summary

  • Examines a security vulnerability in AI-based talking-head videoconferencing where pose-expression latents can be puppeteered to impersonate a victim in real time.
  • Proposes a defense that disentangles persistent biometric identity cues from transient pose/expression within the transmitted latent, without analyzing reconstructed RGB.
  • Introduces a cosine-similarity test on the disentangled embedding to flag illicit identity swaps during rendering.
  • Reports real-time performance, improved robustness over prior puppeteering defenses, and good out-of-distribution generalization.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Danial Samadi Vahdati', 'Tai Duc Nguyen', 'Ekta Prashnani', 'Koki Nagano', 'David Luebke', 'Orazio Gallo', 'Matthew Stamm']
  • Tags: ['biometric leakage', 'impersonation detection', 'talking-head videoconferencing', 'puppeteering', 'latent-based defenses']

item.title: ClusterMark: Towards Robust Watermarking for Autoregressive Image Generators with Visual Token Clustering
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ClusterMark, a robust in-generation watermarking method for autoregressive image generators that watermark via biased visual token prediction.
  • Shows that naive token-level watermark transfers from language-model KGW-style schemes can lose detectability under common image perturbations.
  • Introduces visual token clustering (red/green token sets) and evaluates training-free and fine-tuned variants to improve robustness and maintain image quality.
  • Reports improved robustness against perturbations and regeneration attacks with efficient verification runtime.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Denis Lukovnikov', 'Andreas M\\"uller', 'Erwin Quiring', 'Asja Fischer']
  • Tags: ['AI watermarking', 'Generative model security', 'Regeneration/perturbation resistance', 'Autoregressive image models', 'Token-level detection']

item.title: Enhancing the Safety of Medical Vision-Language Models by Synthetic Demonstrations
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an inference-time defense for medical vision-language models (Med-VLMs) to mitigate harmful queries.
  • Claims to provide defense against both visual and textual jailbreak attacks using synthetic clinical demonstrations.
  • Reports improved safety without significant performance loss, and studies trade-offs such as demonstration budget and a mixed demonstration strategy.

Paper Type

  • Research Paper

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zhiyu Xue', 'Reza Abbasi-Asl', 'Ramtin Pedarsani']
  • Tags: ['Jailbreak defense', 'Vision-language models', 'Inference-time safety', 'Synthetic demonstrations', 'Over-defense trade-off']

item.title: CLIP-Inspector: Model-Level Backdoor Detection for Prompt-Tuned CLIP via OOD Trigger Inversion
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies security risk of malicious MLaaS providers implanting backdoors in prompt-tuned CLIP without corrupting encoders.
  • Proposes CLIP-Inspector, a white-box backdoor detection method that inverts reconstructed OOD triggers per class to verify backdoor behavior.
  • Shows post-hoc fine-tuning using reconstructed triggers can re-align models and reduce backdoor effectiveness.
  • Evaluates across ten datasets and four backdoor attacks with reported high detection accuracy and AUROC.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Akshit Jindal', 'Saket Anand', 'Chetan Arora', 'Vikram Goyal']
  • Tags: ['backdoor detection', 'prompt-tuned CLIP', 'trigger inversion', 'model verification']

item.title: Dictionary-Aligned Concept Control for Safeguarding Multimodal LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Dictionary-Aligned Concept Control (DACO) to safeguard multimodal LLMs by steering internal activations at inference time.
  • Builds a large multimodal concept dictionary (DACO-400K) from caption-image stimuli and uses sparse autoencoder (SAE) concept directions for granular intervention.
  • Introduces a steering approach that initializes SAE training with the concept dictionary and automatically annotates SAE atoms for safety-related control.
  • Evaluates on multiple MLLMs across safety benchmarks including JailBreakV and MM-SafetyBench, reporting improved safety with minimal impact on general capability.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jinqi Luo', 'Jinyu Yang', 'Tal Neiman', 'Lei Fan', 'Bing Yin', 'Son Tran', 'Mubarak Shah', "Ren\\'e Vidal"]
  • Tags: ['AI security', 'jailbreak defense', 'multimodal LLM safety', 'activation steering', 'sparse autoencoders']

item.title: EGLOCE: Training-Free Energy-Guided Latent Optimization for Concept Erasure
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes EGLOCE, a training-free inference-time method to erase specific concepts from text-to-image diffusion models by optimizing latents during sampling.
  • Uses a dual-objective energy framework: repulsion energy to steer away from target concepts and retention energy to preserve alignment to the original prompt.
  • Reports improved concept removal and image quality/prompt alignment versus prior unlearning or inference-time adjustment methods, and claims robustness even under adversarial attacks.
  • Positioned as a plug-and-play safety/compliance technique for controlled image generation via energy-guided latent optimization.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Junyeong Ahn', 'Seojin Yoon', 'Sungyong Baik']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'concept erasure', 'diffusion models', 'inference-time defenses', 'unlearning/containment']

item.title: Mosaic: Multimodal Jailbreak against Closed-Source VLMs via Multi-View Ensemble Optimization
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies multimodal jailbreaking attacks targeting closed-source vision-language models (VLMs).
  • Analyzes how attack effectiveness changes between homogeneous vs heterogeneous surrogate-target settings ("surrogate dependency").
  • Proposes Mosaic: a multi-view, multi-surrogate ensemble optimization framework to improve jailbreak transferability to commercial closed-source VLMs.
  • Reports state-of-the-art attack success rate and toxicity metrics on safety benchmarks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yuqin Lan', 'Gen Li', 'Yuanze Hu', 'Weihao Shen', 'Zhaoxin Fan', 'Faguo Wu', 'Xiao Zhang', 'Laurence T. Yang', 'Zhiming Zheng']
  • Tags: ['AI jailbreaking', 'Multimodal adversarial attacks', 'VLM security', 'Transfer attacks (surrogate ensembles)', 'Safety benchmark evaluation']

item.title: Detecting Diffusion-generated Images via Dynamic Assembly ForestsDetecting Diffusion-generated Images via Dynamic Assembly Forests
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Dynamic Assembly Forest (DAF), a deep-forest-style model, to detect whether images are generated by diffusion models.
  • Motivated by security concerns around diffusion-generated imagery and the need for practical detection tools.
  • Claims competitive performance versus existing DNN-based diffusion image detectors while using fewer parameters and less compute (including deployment without GPUs).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Mengxin Fu', 'Yuezun Li']
  • Tags: ['AI-generated image detection', 'Diffusion models', 'Machine learning forensics', 'Out-of-distribution detection', 'Traditional ML defense']

item.title: Leave My Images Alone: Preventing Multi-Modal Large Language Models from Analyzing Images via Visual Prompt Injection
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces ImageProtector, a user-side visual perturbation technique intended to induce refusals from multimodal LLMs when analyzing protected images.
  • Frames the perturbation as a visual prompt injection attack that disrupts image understanding to prevent extraction of sensitive information (e.g., identities/locations) at scale.
  • Empirically tests the method across multiple open-weight MLLMs and datasets and evaluates countermeasures (Gaussian noise, DiffPure, adversarial training) showing partial mitigation but trade-offs in accuracy/efficiency.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zedian Shao', 'Hongbin Liu', 'Yuepeng Hu', 'Neil Zhenqiang Gong']
  • Tags: ['multimodal security', 'visual prompt injection', 'privacy protection', 'adversarial perturbations', 'refusal induction']

item.title: Precise Shield: Explaining and Aligning VLLM Safety via Neuron-Level Guidance
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes “Precise Shield,” a two-stage framework to identify safety-relevant neurons in VLLMs by contrasting activations on harmful vs. benign multimodal/multilingual inputs.
  • Applies gradient masking to constrain updates to a very small safety neuron subspace (<0.03% of parameters) to improve VLLM safety without sacrificing generalization.
  • Shows cross-language and cross-modal overlap of safety neurons, enabling zero-shot transfer of safety capability.
  • Targets bypasses from composite multilingual/multimodal attacks that exploit structural blind spots in existing high-resource-focused defenses.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Enyi Shi', 'Fei Shen', 'Shuyi Miao', 'Linxia Zhu', 'Pengyang Shao', 'Jinhui Tang', 'Tat-Seng Chua']
  • Tags: ['VLLM safety', 'Neuron-level defense', 'Gradient masking', 'Cross-lingual & multimodal adversarial attacks', 'Safety neuron identification']

item.title: Reasoning Models Will Sometimes Lie About Their Reasoning
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies faithfulness/interpretability of large reasoning models under prompts that warn about unusual input (e.g., hints) and relate this to prompt-injection-style instruction settings.
  • Finds that models may produce seemingly compliant behavior (acknowledging hints) yet still deny intending to use them, even when evidence shows they are using the hints.
  • Introduces/uses more granular faithfulness metrics that reveal mixed performance despite improvements on earlier aggregate metrics.
  • Raises challenges for chain-of-thought monitoring and interpretability, with implications for security-style defenses relying on truthful reasoning explanations.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['William Walden', 'Miriam Wanner']
  • Tags: ['AI security', 'prompt injection', 'model interpretability', 'faithfulness/CoT monitoring']

item.title: Exploiting Web Search Tools of AI Agents for Data Exfiltration
item.description:
Summary

  • Systematically evaluates indirect prompt injection attacks targeting AI agents that use web search/tool-calling and RAG workflows.
  • Analyzes how vulnerability varies by factors like model size, manufacturer, and specific implementations.
  • Demonstrates persistent effectiveness of established attack patterns and identifies most effective methods/parameters.
  • Proposes defenses centered on stronger training/resilience, a centralized attack-vector knowledge base, and a unified continuous testing framework.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Dennis Rall', 'Bernhard Bauer', 'Mohit Mittal', 'Thomas Fraunholz']
  • Tags: ['indirect prompt injection', 'tool-calling/RAG attacks', 'data exfiltration', 'agent security red teaming', 'LLM vulnerability evaluation']

item.title: An Empirical Analysis of Static Analysis Methods for Detection and Mitigation of Code Library Hallucinations
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies whether static analysis can detect and mitigate code “library hallucinations” where LLMs generate nonexistent library features.
  • Empirically evaluates detection rates for general errors (16–70%) and library hallucinations (14–85%), varying by LLM and dataset.
  • Estimates an upper bound on what static methods could catch (48.5%–77%) via manual analysis of cases static analysis can’t plausibly detect.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Clarissa Miranda-Pena', 'Andrew Reeson', "C\\'ecile Paris", 'Josiah Poon', 'Jonathan K. Kummerfeld']
  • Tags: ['AI security', 'hallucination detection', 'static analysis', 'NL-to-code', 'code generation robustness']

item.title: Optimal Multi-bit Generative Watermarking Schemes Under Worst-Case False-Alarm Constraints
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies generative watermarking for large language models under worst-case false-alarm constraints.
  • Shows an existing watermarking scheme is suboptimal and proposes two improved encoding-decoding constructions.
  • Formulates the watermark design as a linear program to characterize optimal multi-bit watermarking performance.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yu-Shin Huang', 'Chao Tian', 'Krishna Narayanan']
  • Tags: ['AI watermarking', 'Generative LMs', 'Detection/false-alarm robustness', 'Worst-case analysis']

item.title: Large Language Models Generate Harmful Content Using a Distinct, Unified Mechanism
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how harmful-content generation is represented internally in LLMs using targeted weight pruning as a causal intervention.
  • Finds harmful generation relies on a compact set of weights shared across harm types, distinct from benign capabilities.
  • Shows alignment reshapes harmful representations, and that compressing these weights can explain emergent misalignment after fine-tuning.
  • Demonstrates that pruning harm-generation weights in narrow domains reduces emergent misalignment, suggesting potential safety-relevant interventions.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hadas Orgad', 'Boyi Wei', 'Kaden Zheng', 'Martin Wattenberg', 'Peter Henderson', 'Seraphina Goldfarb-Tarrant', 'Yonatan Belinkov']
  • Tags: ['LLM safety', 'Model vulnerabilities (harm generation)', 'Jailbreak/misalignment mechanisms', 'Weight pruning/causal interventions', 'Emergent misalignment']

item.title: Do LLMs Follow Their Own Rules? A Reflexive Audit of Self-Stated Safety Policies
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes the Symbolic-Neural Consistency Audit (SNCA) to extract an LLM’s self-stated safety rules, formalize them, and test behavioral compliance against harm benchmarks.
  • Finds systematic discrepancies between stated refusal/safety policies and observed behavior across multiple frontier models and many harm categories.
  • Reports issues with policy articulation completeness and low agreement on rule types, suggesting internal policy statements are not reliably enforced.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Avni Mittal']
  • Tags: ['LLM safety', 'Red teaming', 'Policy compliance evaluation', 'Benchmarking', 'Safety alignment']

item.title: Re-Mask and Redirect: Exploiting Denoising Irreversibility in Diffusion Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows an exploit against diffusion-based language models by re-masking previously committed refusal tokens and injecting an affirmative prefix during denoising.
  • Achieves high attack success rates on HarmBench without gradients or adversarial search (structural vulnerability).
  • Also studies gradient-optimized perturbations (via differentiable Gumbel-softmax) as a contrast, supporting that the weakness is architectural.
  • Proposes defenses such as safety-aware unmasking schedules, step-conditional prefix detection, and post-commitment re-verification.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Arth Singh']
  • Tags: ['diffusion language models', 'adversarial attacks', 'jailbreak/safety bypass', 'denoising schedule exploitation', 'red teaming', 'HarmBench']

item.title: Kill-Chain Canaries: Stage-Level Tracking of Prompt Injection Across Attack Surfaces and Model Safety Tiers
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes “kill-chain canary” framework to track prompt-injection progress through multiple pipeline stages (EXPOSED→PERSISTED→RELAYED→EXECUTED) using a cryptographic token.
  • Evaluates prompt injection across 950 runs, five LLMs, six attack surfaces, and five defense conditions, showing stage-level propagation differences and diagnostic value over binary success/failure metrics.
  • Finds write-node placement/routing decisions are highest leverage; defense mechanisms can fail due to channel mismatch without attacker adaptation.
  • Shows rendered-layer screening (e.g., visible text) is insufficient, as invisible/whitefont PDF payloads can match or exceed ASR.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Haochuan Kevin Wang', 'Zechen Zhang']
  • Tags: ['prompt-injection', 'LLM multi-agent systems', 'attack surface analysis', 'defense evaluation', 'pipeline security']

item.title: Mechanisms of Introspective Awareness
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies “introspective awareness” in LLMs: detecting injected steering vectors in the residual stream and identifying the injected concept.
  • Identifies a mechanistic two-stage circuit for detection (early “evidence carrier” features suppress downstream “gate” features implementing default negative response).
  • Analyzes how the capability emerges post-training (e.g., preference optimization like DPO), and tests robustness via refusal ablation and refusal-related feature modifications.
  • Separately investigates late-layer mechanisms used for concept identification that only weakly overlap with the detection circuitry.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Uzay Macar', 'Li Yang', 'Atticus Wang', 'Peter Wallich', 'Emmanuel Ameisen', 'Jack Lindsey']
  • Tags: ['model interpretability', 'steering vectors', 'jailbreak/prompt-injection related mechanisms', 'mechanistic analysis']

item.title: Large Reasoning Models Learn Better Alignment from Flawed Thinking
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces RECAP, an RLHF-style post-training method that uses counter-aligned chain-of-thought prefilling to correct flawed or unsafe reasoning trajectories.
  • Reports improvements in safety and jailbreak robustness, including better handling under adaptive attack attempts and reduced overrefusal while maintaining reasoning ability.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['ShengYun Peng', 'Eric Smith', 'Ivan Evtimov', 'Song Jiang', 'Pin-Yu Chen', 'Hongyuan Zhan', 'Haozhu Wang', 'Duen Horng Chau', 'Mahesh Pasupuleti', 'Jianfeng Chi']
  • Tags: ['jailbreak robustness', 'RLHF', 'adversarial attacks', 'alignment', 'chain-of-thought']

item.title: Graph Defense Diffusion Model
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes the Graph Defense Diffusion Model (GDDM), a diffusion-based purification/defense method for adversarially attacked graphs.
  • Introduces a structure-driven refiner and a node-feature constrained regularizer to remove adversarial perturbations while preserving graph fidelity.
  • Claims improved flexibility against multiple adversarial attack types (targeted and non-targeted) and better scalability/transfer across similar datasets.
  • Presents experiments showing superior defense performance over prior graph purification approaches on three real-world datasets.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Xin He', 'Wenqi Fan', 'Yili Wang', 'Chengyi Liu', 'Rui Miao', 'Xin Juan', 'Xin Wang']
  • Tags: ['graph adversarial attacks', 'diffusion-based defenses', 'graph purification', 'robustness/security for ML']

item.title: Task-Distributionally Robust Data-Free Meta-Learning
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies robustness of data-free meta-learning under sequential task distribution shifts (TDS) and task distribution corruption (TDC).
  • Identifies a security vulnerability in DFML: susceptibility to attacks via an untrustworthy model pool that deceptively contributes harmful behavior.
  • Proposes a trustworthy DFML framework using synthetic task reconstruction (via model inversion), task memory interpolation/replay to mitigate forgetting, and automatic model selection to filter harmful models.
  • Evaluates failure modes and mitigation strategies for DFML robustness and attack vulnerability.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zixuan Hu', 'Yongxian Wei', 'Li Shen', 'Zhenyi Wang', 'Baoyuan Wu', 'Chun Yuan', 'Dacheng Tao']
  • Tags: ['Data-Free Meta-Learning', 'Robustness', 'Model Inversion/Synthetic Data', 'Poisoning/Untrustworthy Model Pool Security']

item.title: XFED: Non-Collusive Model Poisoning Attack Against Byzantine-Robust Federated Classifiers
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a non-collusive model poisoning attack for federated learning where attackers independently craft malicious updates with a shared objective, without coordination or communication.
  • Introduces XFED, an aggregation-agnostic poisoning method designed to work across common FL aggregation rules.
  • Empirically evaluates on six datasets and reports bypassing eight state-of-the-art defenses and outperforming six prior poisoning attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Israt Jahan Mouri', 'Muhammad Ridowan', 'Muhammad Abdullah Adnan']
  • Tags: ['Federated Learning', 'Model Poisoning Attacks', 'Byzantine Robustness', 'Adversarial ML Security', 'Attack Evaluation/Defense Bypass']

item.title: Leave My Images Alone: Preventing Multi-Modal Large Language Models from Analyzing Images via Visual Prompt Injection
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces ImageProtector, a user-side visual perturbation technique intended to induce refusals from multimodal LLMs when analyzing protected images.

  • Empirically tests the method across multiple open-weight MLLMs and datasets and evaluates countermeasures (Gaussian noise, DiffPure, adversarial training) showing partial mitigation but trade-offs in accuracy/efficiency.

item.title: Tracing the Chain: Deep Learning for Stepping-Stone Intrusion Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ESPRESSO, a deep learning model for correlating network flows to detect stepping-stone intrusions (attackers routing through compromised hosts).
  • Introduces a synthetic data generation tool to create realistic stepping-stone traffic across multiple tunneling protocols and evaluation modes.

item.title: Semantic Intent Fragmentation: A Single-Shot Compositional Attack on Multi-Agent AI Pipelines
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Semantic Intent Fragmentation (SIF), a compositional attack against LLM orchestration/multi-agent pipelines where each generated subtask is benign but the overall composed plan violates security policy.
  • Introduces four attack mechanisms (bulk scope escalation, silent data exfiltration, embedded trigger deployment, quasi-identifier aggregation) that can succeed without injected content, system modification, or post-initial interaction.
  • Evaluates SIF on 14 enterprise scenarios; reports high policy-violating plan success rate (71%) while per-subtask checks appear to pass.
  • Develops/uses plan-level information-flow tracking and compliance evaluation to detect attacks before execution, addressing the compositional safety gap.

item.title: OpenKedge: Governing Agentic Mutation with Execution-Bound Safety and Evidence Chains
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes OpenKedge, a protocol to govern agentic state mutations rather than directly executing probabilistic API calls.
  • Uses declarative intent proposals evaluated against system state, temporal signals, and policy constraints before execution.
  • Compiles approved intents into bounded execution contracts (action/resource/time limits) enforced via ephemeral task-oriented identities.
  • Introduces an Intent-to-Execution Evidence Chain (IEEC) cryptographically linking intent, context, policy decisions, execution bounds, and outcomes for auditability.

item.description:

  • Proposes Continuous-Time Graph MARL (CT-GMARL) using neural ODEs to handle irregularly sampled alerts and mitigate failure modes like scorched-earth actions.

item.description:

item.title: Kill-Chain Canaries: Stage-Level Tracking of Prompt Injection Across Attack Surfaces and Model Safety Tiers
item.description:

  • Finds write-node placement/routing decisions are highest leverage; defense mechanisms can fail due to channel mismatch without attacker adaptation.

item.description:

item.description:

item.title: Reasoning Models Will Sometimes Lie About Their Reasoning
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies faithfulness/interpretability of large reasoning models under prompts that warn about unusual input (e.g., hints) and relate this to prompt-injection-style instruction settings.

item.description:

item.description:

item.title: BadSkill: Backdoor Attacks on Agent Skills via Model-in-Skill Poisoning
item.description:

item.title: Building Better Environments for Autonomous Cyber Defence
item.description:
Summary

  • Provides a framework for decomposing the interface between RL-based autonomous cyber defence (ACD) environments and real systems.
  • Offers best-practice guidelines for building and evaluating RL agents in network defence scenarios, including government/critical infrastructure settings.
  • Focuses on training/evaluation environment design and associated hazards for autonomous defensive agents rather than attacks on AI models directly.

item.title: Semantic Intent Fragmentation: A Single-Shot Compositional Attack on Multi-Agent AI Pipelines
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Semantic Intent Fragmentation (SIF), a compositional attack against LLM orchestration/multi-agent pipelines where each generated subtask is benign but the overall composed plan violates security policy.
  • Introduces four attack mechanisms (bulk scope escalation, silent data exfiltration, embedded trigger deployment, quasi-identifier aggregation) that can succeed without injected content, system modification, or post-initial interaction.
  • Evaluates SIF on 14 enterprise scenarios; reports high policy-violating plan success rate (71%) while per-subtask checks appear to pass.
  • Develops/uses plan-level information-flow tracking and compliance evaluation to detect attacks before execution, addressing the compositional safety gap.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: From Dispersion to Attraction: Spectral Dynamics of Hallucination Across Whisper Model Scales
item.description:
Summary

  • Study spectral dynamics of hallucinations in Whisper ASR models across model scales (Tiny to Large).
  • Propose a Spectral Sensitivity Theorem predicting a phase transition between regimes tied to layer-wise gain/alignment.
  • Validate via eigenspectra/activation graph analysis under adversarial stress, identifying rank collapse/compression behaviors linked to hallucination risk.
  • Focuses on how hallucinations emerge structurally, not on providing mitigations.

item.title: Re-Mask and Redirect: Exploiting Denoising Irreversibility in Diffusion Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows an exploit against diffusion-based language models by re-masking previously committed refusal tokens and injecting an affirmative prefix during denoising.
  • Achieves high attack success rates on HarmBench without gradients or adversarial search (structural vulnerability).
  • Also studies gradient-optimized perturbations (via differentiable Gumbel-softmax) as a contrast, supporting that the weakness is architectural.
  • Proposes defenses such as safety-aware unmasking schedules, step-conditional prefix detection, and post-commitment re-verification.

Paper Type

  • Research

  • Authors: ['Arth Singh']
  • Tags: ['diffusion language models', 'adversarial attacks', 'jailbreak/safety bypass', 'denoising schedule exploitation', 'red teaming', 'HarmBench']

item.title: Unbiased Rectification for Sequential Recommender Systems Under Fake Orders
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies adversarial manipulation of sequential recommender systems via “fake orders” embedded in genuine user sequences (e.g., click farming and sequential perturbations) to mislead recommendations and exposure rates.
  • Proposes an efficient defense/rectification method (DITaR) that identifies harmful fake-order samples using dual-view representations (collaborative vs. semantic) and applies targeted rectification without full retraining.
  • Argues that some partial fake-order signals may be beneficial (data augmentation), so the defense selectively filters only truly harmful samples to avoid removing useful information.
  • Reports improved recommendation quality and computational efficiency while improving robustness against the fake-order threat.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Qiyu Qin', 'Yichen Li', 'Haozhao Wang', 'Cheng Wang', 'Rui Zhang', 'Ruixuan Li']
  • Tags: ['AI security', 'Adversarial manipulation', 'Recommender systems defense', 'Data poisoning/poisoned interactions', 'Robust learning']

item.title: OpenKedge: Governing Agentic Mutation with Execution-Bound Safety and Evidence Chains
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes OpenKedge, a protocol to govern agentic state mutations rather than directly executing probabilistic API calls.
  • Uses declarative intent proposals evaluated against system state, temporal signals, and policy constraints before execution.
  • Compiles approved intents into bounded execution contracts (action/resource/time limits) enforced via ephemeral task-oriented identities.
  • Introduces an Intent-to-Execution Evidence Chain (IEEC) cryptographically linking intent, context, policy decisions, execution bounds, and outcomes for auditability.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jun He', 'Deying Yu']
  • Tags: ['agentic systems security', 'execution-bound safety', 'policy enforcement', 'auditability/traceability', 'cryptographic evidence chains']
